title: Trump Plans to Close and Rebuild a Public Golf Course in Washington
summary:
President Donald Trump has announced plans to renovate East Potomac Golf Links, a public golf course in Washington, D.C., about 2 miles south of the White House. The course sits on national park land.

In a post on Truth Social on Sunday, Trump called the current course "old, broken, dilapidated, and of no further use or effect." He said work will begin on November 15 and the course will close for about 15 months. He shared a plan for a new course he said would be able to host world-class tournaments.

The course has been at the center of a court case for months. In February, a Washington preservation group and two people sued the U.S. Department of the Interior and the National Park Service. They argued that a "championship-style golf course" would raise the cost of playing at a facility that was meant to be "open to all people."

The government argues that the people suing have not shown they were actually harmed. Its lawyers said the plaintiffs' wish for the park service to match their "aesthetic and recreational preferences" is not a legally protected interest.

The federal judge in the case, Ana C. Reyes, ordered the administration to stop cutting down trees at the park. On Friday, the government asked for Reyes to be removed from the case, accusing her of bias. Trump's post did not mention the legal fight.

Skye Perryman, who leads Democracy Forward, a group representing the people suing, said the park "is meant for everyone to enjoy." NPR asked the Interior Department and the White House for comment but had not heard back.

The next court hearing is scheduled for Monday. The golf course is one of several changes Trump is seeking in Washington, including a 250-foot arch near the National Mall.
why_it_matters: The case tests who gets to decide how public park land in the nation's capital is used, and whether it stays affordable for everyone. It also shows how courts can check government plans.

keywords.explanation: To renovate means to repair and update a building or place so it is like new.
Dilapidated describes something old and falling apart from neglect.
Preservation means protecting something, like a historic place, so it is not damaged or changed.
Plaintiffs are the people or groups who bring a lawsuit to court.
A legally protected interest is a right or concern that the law allows a person to defend in court.
Bias means unfairly favoring one side over another.

background_read: The National Park Service, part of the Department of the Interior, manages national park land across the country, including parks in Washington, D.C.
East Potomac Golf Links is a public course on that park land, which means anyone can pay to play there rather than only club members.
When people believe a government plan breaks the law or harms them, they can sue, and a federal judge decides whether the plan can continue.
A judge can order a pause, like stopping tree cutting, while the court case is still being decided.
